verdict.rationale: Cooley runs AI-enabled services, including the firm-owned Cooley AI and prompt-driven S-1 drafting, and Cooley GO collects user inputs in its document generators, so a data-training opt-out is a fair question to ask. However, nothing in the evidence documents any setting, policy or contractual control that keeps user data out of AI model training. The Cyber/Data/Privacy practice is legal advisory work for clients, not a product privacy control, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
